kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the source formulas.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the two formulas, the two definitions, and the two margin rules; the attack structure is a KYP design.

kypExtensions.summary: The two-job reading (LOAD: 'Loading dose = Cp × Vd / F' fills the apparent volume to the target concentration Cp — it depends on Vd and F, not on clearance, which is why 'in renal or liver disease... loading dose is usually unchanged'; MAINTAIN: 'Maintenance dose = Cp × CL × τ / F' replaces each interval τ what clearance CL removes — it depends on CL, τ and F, which is why 'in renal or liver disease, maintenance dose ↓'; with the clock rule 'time to steady state depends primarily on t1/2 and is independent of dose and dosing frequency' and the infusion exclusion 'τ = dosage interval (time between doses); does not apply for continuous infusions') — KYP's synthesis of the page into one decision protocol (which formula, which variable, which dose moves in organ disease).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the two formulas, the two definitions, and the two margin rules as separate text blocks without a unified protocol; the load-vs-maintain framing is KYP's design.

kypExtensions.summary: The four KYP mnemonics (1 — LOAD THE TANK, MAINTAIN THE DRAIN: the formula-selection rule (Vd vs CL); 2 — DIVIDE BY F TO DELIVER: the bioavailability correction shared by both formulas; 3 — SICK ORGANS SHRINK THE MAINTENANCE, SPARE THE LOAD: the renal/liver disease rule; 4 — THE STEADY-STATE CLOCK IS t1/2: the 4-5 half-lives rule with dose-independence). The page prints NO mnemonic in this section — all four codes are KYP-original designs.
kypExtensions.rationale: Book 231's Dosage calculations section prints NO margin mnemonic; all four codes are KYP-original designs.

notes: Census (pdfimages + VLM): NO raster images on the page (pdfimages -list returned zero rows for pdf 253). The Dosage calculations section is pure typeset text: the two fraction formulas ('Loading dose =' with Cp × Vd over F; 'Maintenance dose =' with Cp × CL × τ over F), the two definitions (Cp = target plasma concentration; τ = dosage interval (time between doses); does not apply for continuous infusions), and the two margin rules (In renal or liver disease, maintenance dose ↓ and loading dose is usually unchanged; Time to steady state depends primarily on t1/2 and is independent of dose and dosing frequency). The formulas print in the text layer and are carried verbatim in the note's table blocks and re-typeset as the registry visual's formula panels (ORIGINAL_KYP_ADAPTATION) — short attributed formula phrases, not artwork reproductions. The steady-state accumulation curve drawn in the registry visual (50/75/87.5/93.75/96.9% at 1-5 half-lives) is an ORIGINAL_KYP_REDRAW of the standard first-order accumulation identity — no curve is printed on the source page. The page prints NO margin mnemonic for this section; the KYP memory layer adds four original codes (LOAD THE TANK MAINTAIN THE DRAIN, DIVIDE BY F TO DELIVER, SICK ORGANS SHRINK THE MAINTENANCE, THE STEADY-STATE CLOCK IS t1/2). No copyrighted photographs exist on the page; nothing reproduced. NOTE: page 253 (book 231) ALSO contains the Urine pH and drug elimination section (PH5), already produced and NOT covered by this topic's evidence or visual. NO Drug Metabolism (PH3) or Elimination kinetics (PH4) content appears on this page — those live on pdf 252 (book 230) and are already produced.
